ai.description: Anil's Bush Frog is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It is distinguished by a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes anili* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow-orange iris, which contrasts sharply with the dark, mottled brown coloration of its body.
ai.habitat: Anil's Bush Frog inhabits the high-altitude evergreen rainforests of the Western Ghats, typically found perched on shrubs and trees at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Anil's Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among foliage during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes anili* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon season, laying small clutches in vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes anili* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes anili* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation rainforests.
